title: ADO v2 - Epic forecast
description: Monte Carlo forecast of an Epic, a Feature or a Milestone and of each team against a target date (data set ADOTelemetry.ADOEpicForecastTyped).

panels.title: Chance done by the target date: ${DistTeam:text}
panels.description: Share of simulated futures in which every team has finished its remaining items by the target date (the Epic finishes when its slowest team does). Follows the "Distribution for" selector (whole scope = every team; one team = just that team).

panels.title: Items remaining: ${DistTeam:text}
panels.description: Open, non-removed User Stories and Bugs under the Epic, plus items without a team and the extra items you add. Follows the "Distribution for" selector (whole scope = every team; one team = just that team).

panels.title: P50 weeks
panels.description: Half of the simulated futures finish within this many weeks from today. Follows the "Distribution for" selector (whole scope = every team; one team = just that team).

panels.title: P85 weeks
panels.description: 85% of the simulated futures finish within this many weeks. Follows the "Distribution for" selector (whole scope = every team; one team = just that team).

panels.title: P95 weeks
panels.description: 95% of the simulated futures finish within this many weeks. Follows the "Distribution for" selector (whole scope = every team; one team = just that team).

panels.title: Per team: delivery of the scope by the target date
panels.description: One row per team with remaining Epic items, plus the (Total) row. Weekly mean is the team throughput over the history window (all epics).

panels.title: Remaining work items (open, in scope)
panels.description: Open work items of the chosen scope (Milestone, Epic or Feature), by team. Click the id or title to open the item in Azure DevOps. Removed and done items are not listed. A story without a Feature shows its Epic as 'Epic: ... (no feature)', or '(standalone)' when it has no parent.

options.content:
**Method.** Monte Carlo (bootstrap): each simulated week draws one of the team's real weekly throughputs from the history window; a team is done when its sum reaches its remaining items; the Epic is done when its slowest team is. Counts are User Stories and Bugs, or story points when Unit is Story points (each team measured only against its own points history; unestimated items count as the team average story) (Resolved, IT Tested or Closed = done; Removed = out of scope).

**Assumptions to check.** Items without a team are spread over the teams by their share of the Epic's recent throughput (switch off with *Spread items without a team*). *Extra items* adds work not yet created as stories, spread the same way. *Capacity %* scales every team's throughput (80 = a team delivering 20% less than its history). Scope growth during the period is not simulated; add it through *Extra items*. Skip 1 latest week to ignore the running week.

**Distribution.** The bar chart shows, for the whole scope or the team picked in *Distribution for*, the chance of finishing in each week (the date is the end of that week, counted from today). Red steps finish by P50, orange by P85, yellow by P95, green after P95; the dashed blue vertical line is the target date; steps to its right finish later than the target.

**Data.** `WorkItemScope` from cmf-audit (`--include scope`); only items open or changed since the run's `--since` are known, so keep that at 2026-07-01 or earlier.

**No forecast?** A blank forecast means the scope has no finished items with a team in the history window. Check that the collector passes `--teamFromIterationPath`, raise History weeks, lower Skip latest weeks, or pick a larger scope. Items without a team are spread automatically when the scope has no team at all.

panels.title: Calendar: chance each team is done by week
panels.description: Rows are teams (first row: the whole scope, done when the last team is done), columns are week-ends. Each cell is the chance, from the Monte Carlo, that the team has finished its share of the scope by that date. The outlined column is the target date week.

panels.title: Average weeks
panels.description: Average finish time over all simulated trials, in weeks from today (whole scope). Follows the "Distribution for" selector (whole scope = every team; one team = just that team).

panels.title: Std dev weeks
panels.description: Spread of the simulated finish time, in weeks (whole scope). Smaller means the forecast is more certain. Follows the "Distribution for" selector (whole scope = every team; one team = just that team).

panels.title: Finish date distribution: average, standard deviation and cumulative chance
panels.description: Chance the scope finishes in each week. The blue line is the average finish date and the blue band is plus/minus one standard deviation. Follows the Distribution for selector.

panels.title: Release and deployment calendar (code freeze and planned release)
panels.description: Month view of the upcoming packages. Colour = stream (click a stream in the legend to hide or show it); filled = planned release, outlined = code freeze; red outline and ! = overdue release. Hover for details, click an item to open the Epic forecast for that date.

targets.oDataQueryString: ADOTelemetry.ADOReleasesTyped?$filter=Status ne 'Released' and ('__all' in (${Organization:singlequote}) or Organization in (${Organization:singlequote})) and ('__all' in (${Project:singlequote}) or Project in (${Project:singlequote}))&$select=Version,Line,Stream,Status,CodeFreeze,PlannedRelease,ScheduleChanges&$orderby=CodeFreeze&$top=100

options.css: .rc{display:flex;flex-direction:column;height:100%;font-size:12px}.rc-head{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:6px;margin-bottom:6px;flex-wrap:wrap}.rc-title{font-size:15px;font-weight:600;margin-left:8px}.rc-leg{margin-left:auto;opacity:.85}.rc-b{background:rgba(128,128,128,.15);border:1px solid rgba(128,128,128,.4);color:inherit;border-radius:4px;padding:3px 10px;cursor:pointer}.rc-b:hover{background:rgba(128,128,128,.3)}.rc-d{display:inline-block;width:9px;height:9px;border-radius:2px;margin:0 4px 0 12px;vertical-align:middle}.rc-grid{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(7,1fr);gap:2px;flex:1;min-height:0;grid-auto-rows:auto}.rc-dh{text-align:center;opacity:.7;font-weight:500;padding:2px 0}.rc-c{background:rgba(128,128,128,.08);border:1px solid rgba(128,128,128,.25);border-radius:4px;padding:2px 3px;min-height:64px;overflow:hidden}.rc-c.rc-w{background:rgba(128,128,128,.14)}.rc-c.rc-o{opacity:.45}.rc-c.rc-t{outline:2px solid #5794f2}.rc-n{font-weight:600;opacity:.8;margin-bottom:1px}.rc-e{border-radius:3px;padding:1px 5px;margin:1px 0;color:#111;font-weight:600;white-space:nowrap;overflow:hidden;text-overflow:ellipsis;cursor:pointer}.rc-e:hover{filter:brightness(1.15)}.rc-m{opacity:.7;padding:0 5px}.rc-e.rc-rl{background:var(--c)}.rc-e.rc-fr{background:transparent;color:inherit;border:1px solid var(--c);box-shadow:inset 4px 0 0 var(--c)}.rc-e.rc-ov{outline:2px solid #d44a3a}.rc-s{cursor:pointer;margin-left:10px;white-space:nowrap}.rc-s.off{opacity:.35;text-decoration:line-through}.rc-k{margin-left:14px;opacity:.8}.rc-kf{background:transparent!important;border:1px solid currentColor}.rc-kr{background:currentColor}.rc-foot{margin-top:5px;opacity:.7}

panels.title: Open items in scope without a Feature (relink them in Azure DevOps)
panels.description: Open stories of the chosen scope that sit directly under an Epic or have no parent, so a forecast by Feature cannot select them. The Feature column shows the group they are counted in.
